info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package email is the org's commercial mail: one message sent through the org's own SES or SendGrid account (POST /v1/email), the ledger of every message and the provider events that report on it, kept in the org's Base, and address verification.

get.summary: Reads a page of the org's ledger, newest first: every message sent through POST /v1/email, and every message SES or SendGrid told of by its events, sent from anywhere on the org's account.
get.description:
Reads a page of the org's ledger, newest first: every message sent
through POST /v1/email, and every message SES or SendGrid told of by its events,
sent from anywhere on the org's account. It narrows by status, provider, a range
of send time (since, until) and one recipient, and pages by cursor: pass the
answer's next to read the page after.

GET /v1/email

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit is the most messages on the page (default 50, max 200).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Status is one status to list: queued, sent, failed, delivered, opened,
clicked, bounced or complained.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Since is the earliest send time listed, RFC 3339.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Until is the send time listing stops before, RFC 3339.

parameters.name: recipient
parameters.description: Recipient lists the messages to one address.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Cursor is the next of the page before; empty is the newest page.

post.summary: Sends commercial email from the org through SES or SendGrid: one message per recipient, each carrying its own signed unsubscribe link in the footer and in List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post (RFC 8058), and every http(s) link tagged with utm_source=email, utm_medium=<provider>, utm_campaign=<campaign>, utm_content=link<n> and from=<message id>, each only where the link does not carry it already.
post.description:
Sends commercial email from the org through SES or SendGrid: one
message per recipient, each carrying its own signed unsubscribe link in the
footer and in List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post (RFC 8058), and every
http(s) link tagged with utm_source=email, utm_medium=<provider>,
utm_campaign=<campaign>, utm_content=link<n> and from=<message id>, each only
where the link does not carry it already. Every recipient is first asked of the
one suppression check (marketing_clearance): an address the org's list holds,
whose company unsubscribed, or that the platform blocks is not sent to, and is
answered in refused with status 422 and the reason; when every recipient is
refused the request is 422. A list that cannot answer sends nothing (503).

The rail is the provider the request pins (ses or sendgrid), else the org's
default (PUT /v1/email/provider), else SES, else SendGrid, whichever the org
holds credentials for; anything else is 400. Every message is kept in the org's
ledger (GET /v1/email), counted (GET /v1/email/stats), stated on the event
stream as email_sent, and put on the CRM record of the person the org holds for
the address. The same idempotency key and recipient send once. Transactional
mail (a code, a receipt) is not this route's: it goes by /v1/notify, which no
opt-out stops.

POST /v1/email

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
IdempotencyKey names the send, so a retried request sends each recipient's
message once: the same key and recipient name the same message.

put.summary: Sets the provider the org's mail leaves by when a send pins none: ses or sendgrid.
put.description:
Sets the provider the org's mail leaves by when a send pins none:
ses or sendgrid. With none set it is SES, else SendGrid, whichever the org holds
credentials for; a send that pins one goes by it. Org admin only, and on the
audit trail (email.provider.set) before it takes effect.

PUT /v1/email/provider

get.summary: Reports the org's SendGrid configuration: whether it holds the credentials a send needs, the account's credits as SendGrid answers them, what the org's ledger counted sent by SendGrid in the last 24 hours, and the DNS records of the sending domain.
get.description:
Reports the org's SendGrid configuration: whether it holds the
credentials a send needs, the account's credits as SendGrid answers them, what
the org's ledger counted sent by SendGrid in the last 24 hours, and the DNS
records of the sending domain.

GET /v1/email/sendgrid/status

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain is an optional sending domain to generate SendGrid whitelabel DKIM, Return-Path, and DMARC records for.

get.summary: Reports the org's Amazon SES configuration: whether it holds the credentials a send needs, the account's limits as SES answers them (sandbox, sending enabled, 24-hour quota, rate, sent in the last 24 hours), what the org's ledger counted sent by SES in the last 24 hours, and the DNS records of the sending domain.
get.description:
Reports the org's Amazon SES configuration: whether it holds the
credentials a send needs, the account's limits as SES answers them (sandbox,
sending enabled, 24-hour quota, rate, sent in the last 24 hours), what the org's
ledger counted sent by SES in the last 24 hours, and the DNS records of the
sending domain.

GET /v1/email/ses/status

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain optionally specifies the sending domain to generate Easy DKIM and MAIL FROM records for.

get.summary: Counts the org's mail over a range: sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced, complained and unsubscribed, each a count of messages, in all, by provider, by campaign and by day or hour (UTC).
get.description:
Counts the org's mail over a range: sent, delivered, opened, clicked,
bounced, complained and unsubscribed, each a count of messages, in all, by
provider, by campaign and by day or hour (UTC). Mail sent around this API, from
the org's own tools on its SES or SendGrid account, is counted from the
providers' events like mail sent through it.

GET /v1/email/stats

parameters.name: since
parameters.description:
Since is where the range starts, RFC 3339, rounded down to its day or hour.
Empty is 30 days before Until by day, 48 hours by hour.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description:
Until is where the range ends, RFC 3339, rounded up to its day or hour.
Empty is now.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Interval is day (default, at most 400 days) or hour (at most 31 days), in UTC.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Provider counts one rail only: ses or sendgrid.

post.summary: Evaluates an email address using explicitly selected, composable checks.
post.description:
Evaluates an email address using explicitly selected, composable checks.

A signed-in caller only: the SMTP check connects to the address's mail server
from ours, so an anonymous caller could probe mailboxes and get our addresses
blocked. Each caller may run 120 checks an hour and 20 of them SMTP probes, and
the deployment 6,000 and 400; past either is 429.

POST /v1/email/verify

post.summary: Receives SendGrid's Signed Event Webhook: the delivery is an array of events, signed (ECDSA P-256, SHA-256) over its timestamp header followed by the body, under the public key the organization holds (the webhook-public-key credential).
post.description:
Receives SendGrid's Signed Event Webhook: the delivery is an
array of events, signed (ECDSA P-256, SHA-256) over its timestamp header
followed by the body, under the public key the organization holds
(the webhook-public-key credential). A delivery signed more than ten minutes
from now is refused, so a captured one cannot be replayed.

POST /v1/email/webhooks/sendgrid?org=<org>

post.summary: Receives Amazon SES events as an SNS HTTPS subscription delivers them.
post.description:
Receives Amazon SES events as an SNS HTTPS subscription delivers
them. The organization is named in the address (?org=) and holds the SNS topic
its events arrive on (the sns-topic-arn credential): a message is accepted when
it is signed by SNS, is from that topic, and its certificate comes from that
topic's region. A subscription confirmation is completed the same way and
records nothing.

POST /v1/email/webhooks/ses?org=<org>

get.summary: Reads one message of the org's ledger, sent through this API or told of by its provider, with what became of it.
get.description:
Reads one message of the org's ledger, sent through this API or told of
by its provider, with what became of it.

GET /v1/email/:id

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is our id for the message (msg_…).

disposable.description: Disposable reports whether the domain belongs to a temporary or throwaway provider.

free.description: Free reports whether the domain belongs to a free consumer webmail provider.

reason.description: Reason describes the failure or skip reason when Status is not pass.

role.description: Role reports whether the address is a generic role or distribution account.

status.description: Status reports the check outcome: pass, fail, unknown, or skipped.

messages.description:
Messages is one message per recipient that was sent, each with its own
unsubscribe link; a message the provider refused is here with status failed.

refused.description:
Refused is every recipient the suppression check refused. Nothing was sent
to them.

reason.description: Reason describes the failure or skip reason when Status is not pass.

status.description: Status reports the check outcome: pass, fail, unknown, or skipped.

next.description: Next is the cursor of the page after this one; empty on the last page.

reason.description: Reason describes the failure or skip reason when Status is not pass.

records.description: Records lists the discovered mail exchanger hostnames.

status.description: Status reports the check outcome: pass, fail, unknown, or skipped.

bounce.description: Bounce is hard or soft, for a message that bounced.

bounced_at.description: BouncedAt is when it bounced, and Bounce whether hard or soft.

campaign.description: Campaign is the campaign the message was tagged with.

clicked_at.description: ClickedAt is when a link in it was first clicked.

complained_at.description: ComplainedAt is when its recipient reported it as spam.

created_at.description: CreatedAt is when the message was sent, or accepted to be.

delivered_at.description: DeliveredAt is when the receiving server first took it.

error.description: Error says why it failed, bounced, was deferred or was rejected.

from.description: From is the sender address, when known.

id.description:
ID is our id for the message (msg_…): every link in it carries it as from=,
and the event stream names it by it.

idempotency_key.description: IdempotencyKey is the key the message was sent under.

opened_at.description: OpenedAt is when it was first opened.

org.description: Org is the organization owning this message.

origin.description:
Origin is api for a message POST /v1/email sent, provider for one the
provider's events told of, sent from the org's own tools.

provider.description: Provider is the rail it went by: ses or sendgrid.

provider_id.description:
ProviderID is the provider's own id for the message, which its events name
it by; empty until the provider answers one.

status.description:
Status is queued, sent, failed, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced or
complained.

subject.description: Subject is the message subject line, when known.

unsubscribed_at.description: UnsubscribedAt is when its recipient unsubscribed from it.

name.description: Name is the provider (ses, sendgrid) or the campaign.

tally.description: Tally is its mail counted over the range.

at.description: At is the start of the day or hour, UTC.

reason.description:
Reason is why: unsubscribed, company unsubscribed (the address's domain
opted out of the org's mail) or blocklisted (the platform's list).

status.description: Status is 422: the address may not be mailed.

host.description: Host is the DNS record host or subdomain name.

priority.description: Priority is the MX priority when Type is MX.

purpose.description: Purpose describes the role of the DNS record (e.g. DKIM, MAIL FROM MX, MAIL FROM SPF, DMARC).

type.description: Type is the DNS record type (CNAME, MX, TXT).

value.description: Value is the DNS record target or text value.

verified.description: Verified reports whether the DNS record is verified for the sending identity.

active_provider.description: ActiveProvider is the provider the org's mail leaves by when a request pins none.

configuration_set.description:
ConfigurationSet is the SES configuration set messages go out under, whose
event destination publishes their events (hanzo-crm-events unless the
credential names another).

configured.description:
Configured reports whether the org holds the SES credentials a send needs
(access-key-id, secret-access-key, from-email).

dns_records.description: DNSRecords lists the Easy DKIM, SPF, MX, and DMARC records for the sending domain.

domain.description: Domain is the sending domain inspected.

from_email.description: FromEmail is the default verified sender address.

from_name.description: FromName is the default sender display name.

mail_from_domain.description: MailFromDomain is the custom MAIL FROM subdomain (bounce.<domain>).

max_24_hour_send.description: Max24HourSend is the account's 24-hour sending quota, as SES answers it.

max_send_rate.description: MaxSendRate is the account's most messages a second, as SES answers it.

provider_sent_last_24_hours.description:
ProviderSentLast24Hours is what SES counts sent by the account in the last
24 hours, from anywhere.

quota_error.description:
QuotaError says why the account's limits could not be read; the limits are
then 0.

region.description: Region is the configured Amazon SES AWS region (defaults to us-east-1).

sandbox.description: Sandbox is whether SES says the account is still in its sandbox.

sending_enabled.description: SendingEnabled is whether SES says the account may send.

sent_last_24_hours.description:
SentLast24Hours is what the org's ledger counts sent by SES in the last 24
hours: through POST /v1/email, and every message SES's events told of.

catch_all.description: CatchAll reports whether the host accepts all recipient addresses.

deliverable.description: Deliverable reports whether the mailbox accepted the test recipient address.

disabled.description: Disabled reports whether the recipient mailbox is disabled or inactive.

full_inbox.description: FullInbox reports whether the recipient mailbox is over quota.

host_exists.description: HostExists reports whether the destination mail server host exists and responded.

reason.description: Reason describes the failure or skip reason when Status is not pass.

status.description: Status reports the check outcome: pass, fail, unknown, or skipped.

active_provider.description: ActiveProvider is the provider the org's mail leaves by when a request pins none.

asm_group_id.description: ASMGroupID is the optional SendGrid suppression group ID.

configured.description:
Configured reports whether the org holds the SendGrid credentials a send
needs (api-key, from-email).

credits_remaining.description: CreditsRemaining is the credits left in the period.

credits_total.description:
CreditsTotal, CreditsRemaining and CreditsUsed are the account's sending
credits for the period, as SendGrid answers them.

credits_used.description: CreditsUsed is the credits used in the period.

dns_records.description: DNSRecords lists the required SendGrid Domain Authentication CNAME, Link Branding, SPF, and DMARC DNS records.

domain.description: Domain is the sending domain used for SendGrid Domain Authentication and DMARC.

from_email.description: FromEmail is the configured SendGrid outreach sender email address.

from_name.description: FromName is the configured SendGrid outreach sender display name.

ip_pool.description: IPPool is the SendGrid IP pool the credential names, if any.

quota_error.description: QuotaError says why the account's credits could not be read; they are then 0.

reply_to.description: ReplyTo is the configured Reply-To address for outreach replies.

sent_last_24_hours.description:
SentLast24Hours is what the org's ledger counts sent by SendGrid in the last
24 hours: through POST /v1/email, and every message SendGrid's events told of.

separate_from_twilio_notify.description: SeparateFromTwilioNotify confirms that SendGrid outreach uses its own dedicated API key, sender identity, and IP pool distinct from standard Twilio transactional notifications.

body.description: Body is an alias for Text for backward compatibility.

campaign.description:
Campaign tags the messages: 1 to 128 letters, digits, '-' or '_', which is
what an SES message tag may hold. Every link carries it as utm_campaign, the
provider carries it back on every event, and the stats count by it.

from.description: From is the sender address. If empty, the provider credential's from-email is used.

headers.description: Headers provides optional custom MIME headers.

idempotency_key.description:
IdempotencyKey names the send, so a retried request sends each recipient's
message once: the same key and recipient name the same message.

provider.description:
Provider pins the rail, ses or sendgrid. Empty is the org's default
(PUT /v1/email/provider), else ses, else sendgrid, whichever the org holds
credentials for.

sync.description: Sync is accepted for backwards compatibility with notify sends.

template_id.description: TemplateID optionally references a built-in template.

template_vars.description: TemplateVars carries variables for template rendering.

text.description: Text is the plain text body.

to.description: To lists destination recipient addresses. Each gets a message of its own.

campaign.description: Campaign is the one campaign counted, when the request named one.

campaigns.description:
Campaigns is the range by campaign, the most sent first, at most 200; empty
when the request named a campaign.

interval.description: Interval is day or hour: the step of Series.

provider.description: Provider is the one rail counted, when the request named one.

providers.description: Providers is the range by provider.

series.description: Series is every day or hour of the range in order, empty ones included.

since.description: Since is the start of the range, UTC.

until.description: Until is the end of the range, UTC, not included.

email.description: Email is the suggested alternative address.

reason.description: Reason describes why the suggestion was made (e.g. domain_typo).

domain.description: Domain is the domain-part of the email address.

reason.description: Reason describes the failure or skip reason when Status is not pass.

status.description: Status reports the check outcome: pass, fail, unknown, or skipped.

username.description: Username is the local-part of the email address.

bounced.description: Bounced is messages that bounced, hard or soft (SendGrid's dropped included).

clicked.description: Clicked is messages a link of which was clicked.

complained.description: Complained is messages reported as spam.

delivered.description: Delivered is messages the receiving server took.

sent.description: Sent is messages the provider accepted.

unsubscribed.description: Unsubscribed is messages whose recipient unsubscribed at the provider.

classification.description: Classification details account attributes (disposable, free, role).

domain.description: Domain details DNS domain host resolution.

mx.description: MX details DNS mail exchanger lookup.

checks.description:
Checks explicitly selects which checks to run.
Defaults to ["syntax", "domain", "mx", "classification"].

email.description: Email is the address to evaluate.

from_email.description: FromEmail sets sender used in MAIL FROM for SMTP probe when explicitly enabled.

hello_name.description: HelloName sets domain used in EHLO for SMTP probe when explicitly enabled.

proxy_uri.description: ProxyURI sets optional proxy for network lookups.

suggestions.description: Suggestions requests domain typo suggestions without altering the original email.

checks.description: Checks contains the outcomes of all requested checks.

email.description: Email is the original submitted email address.

suggestions.description: Suggestions lists potential corrections when requested.

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
